subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: For Codex OAuth sibling-model failover, should OpenClaw keep Codex models on the app-server and pursue the suspected upstream websocket/rate-limit bug, or add direct-runtime Codex Harmony tool-call support so direct OpenClaw routing becomes a supported fallback?
rationale: Both paths are plausible, but the choice changes runtime ownership, provider routing, and tool-call parsing behavior; the exact app-server false-429 cause still needs live Codex quota proof.

options.title: Investigate app-server first
options.body: Keep app-server as the default Codex runtime, review the narrower bookkeeping PR, and require live proof of the suspected upstream websocket/rate-limit context bug before changing routing.

options.title: Support direct Codex routing
options.body: Add a Codex Harmony tool-call adapter to the direct OpenAI responses runtime and then consider a deliberate direct-runtime fallback for Codex OAuth models.

options.title: Wait for stronger repro
options.body: Leave the issue open until a maintainer or reporter provides redacted live logs or a trace proving which runtime layer returns the unexpected 429.

recommendation.title: Investigate app-server first
recommendation.body: Keep app-server as the default Codex runtime, review the narrower bookkeeping PR, and require live proof of the suspected upstream websocket/rate-limit context bug before changing routing.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent OpenAI provider identity, direct runtime extraction, and Codex model support work put them closest to the runtime-direction decision.
